title: Independent ideas. Extraordinary finds.
intro: A daily selection of independent games and useful Android apps, with original F7 insights and links to their creators.

entries.name: Warzone 2100
entries.summary: Warzone 2100 is a free 3D real-time strategy game from the Warzone 2100 Project. You lead the forces of The Project after nuclear missiles have nearly destroyed humanity, taking ground, gathering resources, and growing bases through production and research. Matches can be played alone or with other people on a local network or online. Installers are published for Windows, macOS, and Linux.
features: Lead The Project in a 3D campaign set after a nuclear war.
Capture territory and resources, then expand bases, production, and research.
Join LAN or online battles for as many as 10 players.
Install official builds for Windows, macOS, and Linux.
entries.insight: The base-building loop is tied to a world that has to be rebuilt, so expansion feels like recovery rather than a generic skirmish. For F7, it is a clear example of a fully free strategy game that still offers large multiplayer battles.

entries.name: Flare: Empyrean Campaign
entries.summary: Flare: Empyrean Campaign is a free 2D action role-playing game by the Flare team. The story starts with exile from Empyrean and follows a journey back through several regions and optional side quests. The team describes the fantasycore art as dark fantasy, with violence and some blood. Windows, macOS, and Linux downloads include both the engine and the game.
features: Begin exiled from Empyrean and quest for a way to return.
Travel through multiple regions, with side quests along the route.
Play a 2D action RPG on the free Flare engine.
Download Windows, macOS, and Linux packages that bundle the engine and game.
entries.insight: Exile gives the combat a destination: each region is a step toward getting home, and the side quests let that journey wander. F7 likes that the same team ships both the engine and a complete campaign other people can still mod.

entries.name: Red Eclipse
entries.summary: Red Eclipse is a free arena shooter by Quinton Reeves and Lee Salzman. Movement is the main skill: parkour, impulse boosts, and dashing sit alongside arena combat. Players can change matches with a large set of mutators, and maps can be built together in a real-time cooperative editor. Packages are offered for Windows, Linux, BSD, and macOS.
features: Move with parkour, impulse boosts, dashing, and other agility tricks.
Change matches using a large set of mutators and game variables.
Build maps with other players in a real-time cooperative editor.
Download official packages for Windows, Linux, BSD, and macOS.
entries.insight: Most arena shooters ask you to aim first. Red Eclipse asks you to arrive first, then aim. That parkour-led pace, plus a cooperative map editor, makes it a strong find for players who want a match they can also reshape.

entries.name: Xonotic
entries.summary: Xonotic is a free arena shooter from Team Xonotic for Windows, macOS, and Linux. It ships with a large weapon set, each gun having a primary and secondary fire, and modes that run from deathmatch and capture the flag to race, Nexball, and freeze tag. Twenty-five official maps are included, and an editor ships with the game. Player statistics through XonStat are optional and do not require an account.
features: Choose among 9 core weapons and 16 full weapons, each with two firing modes.
Play deathmatch, capture the flag, clan arena, race, Nexball, and freeze tag.
Start with 25 official maps and open the included editor to make more.
Track optional XonStat results, including accuracy, without creating a login.
entries.insight: Xonotic keeps the arena-shooter promise of fast rooms, distinct weapons, and modes you can learn in one match, while leaving statistics off until a player asks for them. F7 sees a complete shooter that does not hide those modes behind a store page.

entries.name: Fossify Calendar
entries.summary: Fossify Calendar is an Android calendar for events and reminders stored on the device. It offers day, week, month, year, and event-list views, plus recurring events, holidays, and home-screen widgets. You can import and export calendar data. The app does not request Android's Internet permission, and Fossify does not run its own calendar sync service.
features: Plan events in day, week, month, year, and event-list views.
Add recurring events, reminders, holidays, and celebrations.
Import and export calendar data and pin schedule widgets.
Keep calendar data local; the app does not request Internet permission.
entries.insight: A calendar that can show the whole month and still export the data is the practical pair. F7 likes that reminders and widgets are here without a Fossify account sitting in the middle.

entries.name: Fossify Keyboard
entries.summary: Fossify Keyboard is an Android keyboard that types offline. It includes multiple languages and layouts, numbers, symbols, emoji, and clipboard snippets for text you reuse. Typed text is delivered to the app you are using and is not sent to Fossify. The current release is marked beta, and the app does not request Internet permission.
features: Type offline with multiple languages, layouts, numbers, and symbols.
Insert emoji and saved clipboard snippets.
Adjust typing preferences, vibration, and the theme.
Keep keystrokes on the device; the app does not request Internet permission.
entries.insight: A replacement keyboard is present in every app, so an offline design matters. F7 would rather keep snippets and layouts on the device than send typing to a suggestion service.

entries.name: Fossify Music Player
entries.summary: Fossify Music Player plays music files already stored on an Android device. You can browse by album, artist, genre, and folder, then use a queue, shuffle, repeat, an equalizer, and a sleep timer. Home-screen widgets and lock-screen controls are included. It does not require a streaming account, and it does not request Internet permission.
features: Play local albums, artists, songs, and playlists without a streaming account.
Control the queue, shuffle, repeat, equalizer, and a sleep timer.
Browse the library by album, artist, genre, and folder.
Use home-screen widgets and lock-screen controls while playback stays offline.
entries.insight: A local library still needs a queue and a sleep timer, not only a file list. Music Player covers that path for people who already keep the songs on the device.

entries.name: Fossify Notes
entries.summary: Fossify Notes keeps text notes and checklists on Android, with home-screen widgets so a list stays visible. Individual notes can be locked, and the app can import, export, or automatically back up its data. There is no account to create. The release is marked beta, and the app does not request Internet permission.
features: Write text notes, shopping lists, and checklists.
Pin notes to the home screen with widgets.
Lock the app or a note, with fingerprint as an option.
Import, export, and optionally back up notes without signing in.
entries.insight: A shopping list should not require an account. Fossify Notes stays on the phone, puts the list on the home screen, and still gives you a file you can export.

entries.name: Fossify Messages
entries.summary: Fossify Messages is an Android SMS and MMS app. It handles one-to-one and group conversations, search, blocking, and importing or exporting blocked numbers. You can back up and restore message history, schedule a message, and send a quick reply. The stable release is linked from Google Play, F-Droid, and GitHub.
features: Send SMS and MMS, including group conversations.
Search conversations, block numbers, and move blocked-number lists.
Back up and restore message history.
Schedule messages and send quick replies.
entries.insight: Search and a backup matter once a message history gets long. F7 likes that scheduling and blocking sit in the same local SMS app.

entries.name: NewPipe
entries.summary: NewPipe is a free Android app for YouTube and PeerTube. It avoids proprietary Google APIs, lets you choose a resolution, and can save video, audio, or captions for offline playback. Videos can keep playing in the background or in a movable popup. Subscriptions, playlists, bookmarks, and history stay on the device. Team NewPipe distributes it on F-Droid and through GitHub releases.
features: Watch YouTube and PeerTube and choose the resolution and file format.
Save video, audio, or captions for offline playback.
Keep playing in a background audio player or a movable popup.
Store subscriptions, playlists, bookmarks, and history on the device.
entries.insight: Background audio and a popup player cover the two ways people keep a video going while doing something else. F7 likes that those tools sit next to on-device subscriptions, so the useful parts do not depend on a store account.

entries.name: DAVx⁵

price.label: Paid on Google Play; free F-Droid builds

entries.summary: DAVx⁵ syncs contacts, calendars, and tasks between Android and CalDAV, CardDAV, and WebDAV servers. Address books can include photos, groups, and shared read-only books. Calendars keep recurring events, invitations, and time zones. WebDAV folders can be browsed and edited directly, including more than one cloud. bitfire charges a fee on Google Play and also points to free F-Droid builds.
features: Sync contacts, including photos, groups, and shared address books.
Sync calendars with recurring events, invitations, and time zones.
Browse, edit, and stream files from one or more WebDAV clouds.
Choose the paid Google Play build or a free F-Droid build.
entries.insight: Phone calendars and address books are more useful when they can live on a server you choose. DAVx⁵ is that bridge, including shared books and recurring events, while the phone's own calendar and contacts apps stay in place.
